passages.note: Campaign issues page written in the third person ("She fully supports ... deporting criminal illegal aliens"); not her own words, and silent on everyone other than criminals.
Praises detention and deportation of 'dangerous illegal aliens' under the Laken Riley Act; shows the enforcement side but states neither 'only' (rung 2) nor 'all' (rungs 4-5).
The Dalilah Law limits commercial driver's licenses to lawfully present people; it does not say who should be deported.
Yea on final passage of the Laken Riley Act (263-156, not near-unanimous); a detention mandate for people charged with listed crimes shows the enforcement side only (annex rung 2 note).
passages.actor_quote: Houchin Houchin Republican Indiana IN Yea

passages.provision_quote: is charged with, is arrested for, is convicted of, admits having committed, or admits committing acts which constitute the essential elements of any burglary, theft, larceny, shoplifting, or assault of a law enforcement officer offense
passages.note: Operative section mandates detention of people charged with (not only convicted of) theft-type and other crimes; it sets no rule for removing everyone else, so it separates no rungs on the enforcement side.

rows.reasoning: Her Yea on the Laken Riley Act (S. 5, 119th) mandates detention of people charged with listed crimes, and her own words praise that dangerous illegal aliens are 'detained and deported'; both show the enforcement side but neither limits removal to 'only ... serious violent crimes' nor calls to 'deport all undocumented immigrants', so no single rung is established.

quotes.text: Thanks to the Laken Riley Act, dangerous illegal aliens are finally being detained and deported before they can commit more crimes.
